summary: Charles Goodman works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan in 2002 under Allan Gibbard and was an associate professor at Binghamton University as of 2013.

Charles H. Long was a religious studies scholar who earned his BD and PhD from the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago (1956–1974), UNC and Duke (1974–1986), Syracuse (1986–1990), and UC Santa Barbara (circa 1990–1996).

Charles Hallisey is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Colgate, Harvard, UPenn, and the University of Chicago (PhD 1988). He held faculty posts at Loyola Chicago, Harvard, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Charles Hamilton was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He served in the military with the East India Company starting in 1776 and became one of the first members of The Asiatic Society (circa 1784–1792).

Charles Harris was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Indiana University and under Ernst Windisch at the University of Leipzig (PhD 1884), later serving as Professor of German at Oberlin (1888–1893) and Case Western Reserve (1893).

Charles Henry Allan Bennett worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He founded the Buddhasasana Samagama and The Buddhist Review, and headed the Buddhist Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1908.

Charles Henry Tawney was an Indologist educated at Trinity College, Cambridge. He held professorial and leadership roles at Presidency University (1864–1892), served as Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1880), and was Librarian at the India Office (1893–1903).

Charles Hubert Biddulph was an Indology and history/archaeology researcher. He studied at Philander Smith College and Crystal Palace School of Engineering, later working as an engineer and Deputy General Manager for the South Indian Railway Company (1924–1966).
Charles Hyart was a linguist who studied under René Fohalle at the University of Liège from circa 1931 to 1935. He later taught Russian at the University of Liège from circa 1945 to 1983.

Charles James Lyall was a linguist and Indologist educated at King's College London and Balliol College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Civil Service (circa 1867–1898) and as Professor of Arabic at Oxford (1913–1920).

Charles James Rodgers was an Indologist and historian educated at Borough Road College and Cambridge. He was Principal at Amritsar's Christian Vernacular Education Society Training College (1863) and Honorary Numismatist for the Government of India (circa 1886–1892).

Charles Johnston worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (circa 1884–1888) and served as a Special Lecturer in Political Science at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1908.

Charles Jones Ogden studied Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies at Columbia University under A. V. Williams Jackson. He later served as Columbia's Honorary Lecturer in Indo-Iranian Languages from 1926 to 1931.
Charles Lecoutere was a linguist who earned his PhD at KU Leuven under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin (circa 1888–1892). He became a professor at KU Leuven in 1895.
Charles Li works in Indology, philosophy, and computational fields. After earning a PhD at Cambridge (2014–2018), he held posts at UBC, the CNRS (2020–2023), and the University of Hamburg (2023).

Charles Louis Fabri was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Pécs, Leiden under Jean Philippe Vogel, and Paris under Sylvain Lévi. He held posts with the Archaeological Survey of India, Lahore Museum, and National Museum, New Delhi.

Charles Malamoud is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris. He held academic posts at the University of Lyon (circa 1962–1972) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (circa 1978–1998).
Charles Masson was an Indology and history/archaeology figure who served as an agent for the East India Company from circa 1821 to 1826 and for the Government of India from circa 1835 to 1838.

Charles Matthew Whish was an Indologist and historian who trained at East India Company College and the College of Fort St. George. He worked as a civil servant for the Madras Presidency and East India Company (1812–1833).

Charles Michel was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Félix Nève at KU Leuven and Abel Bergaigne at Paris. He served as a professor at Ghent University (1885–1892) and the University of Liège (1892–1923).
